title: Protocols: FTP and SFTP, SSL and TLS, LDAP and LDAPS

videos.script: Many protocols in daily use were designed before anybody encrypted anything. Each now has a secure twin, and the two often sit side by side on the same server. {{title}} FTP sends the password exactly as it was typed. {{ftp}} SFTP runs over SSH, so the password, or better the key, travels inside an encrypted channel, and the server proves who it is first. {{sftp}} LDAP, the directory behind most company logins, has the same split. Plain on port 389, encrypted as LDAPS on 636, or upgraded in place with StartTLS. {{ldap}} The secure twin only helps if the insecure one is switched off. This lesson shows each pair in the lab, and a server refusing the unsafe way in. {{refuse}}
